brief_extract: The E.A.W. All-Electric House opened at Bristol in October, photographs of which are reproduced in this number, is an embodiment of inter-dependent electrical service and labour-saving design which it is hoped will eventually be followed by architects and builders in comparative degree for all types of homes. Women should and do have a very pertinent interest in improvement of living conditions, but in some ways the individual carries less weight to-day than in the past, and it is by collective efforts that great developments may best be accomplished.

location_standardised: Great Britain, United Kingdom
brief_context: Described as the pioneer in public electricity supply.
brief_extract: The answer goes back a long way. Great Britain was the pioneer in public electricity supply, as in so many other modern developments, and in the early days transmission of electricity over long distances was technically impracticable. This encouraged the setting up of a large number of small separate supply authorities, and by the time alternating current was introduced and long-distance transmission became practicable there had been created a tragic muddle of restricted areas and small inefficient rapidly out-dated stations, and a bewildering medley of technical systems.

location_standardised: Great Britain, United Kingdom
brief_context: The Grid district schemes cover the whole of Great Britain.
brief_extract: The 1926 Act laid upon the Central Electricity Board the duty of first constructing and then operating the Grid. Appointed in 1927, the Board has adopted nine district schemes, covering the whole of Great Britain except North Scotland, and accounting for some 98% of the population. Six years after construction began, the initial stage of construction was practically complete.

location_standardised: Geneva, Canton de Genève, Switzerland
brief_context: Mentioned as part of political discussions in a salon.
brief_extract: Intelligent women, journalists, writers, doctors, belaboured me with arguments. I was beginning to hate the sounds of the words “Le Home Fleet— Monsieur Eden — Geneva.” Having neither an inexhaustible French vocabulary nor the type of nose that can register aloofness by a voluntary change of angle, I was at times in a tight corner. Then came the brochure, and Anglo-French friction, a thing after all mostly of words, was forgotten.

location_standardised: France

brief_extract: Columns appear in the Press, and for a day or two your house is the object of much interest. A wholly electric house was therefore bound to cause excitement, and a house designed by women for women at a price which, even in financially stricken France would seem extremely low, was certain to prove a subject for discussion. It did.

location_standardised: Southern France, France
brief_context: Region where the author stayed in an electrical hotel.
brief_extract: But in spite of all-electric houses and familiarity with electricity as an everyday friend, I have not yet become so electrically blasé that I cannot be thrilled by minor manifestations of this wonder in our midst. Hence having recently to unpack my trunks in the noisiest, dreariest town in the South of France, I was delighted to find myself in the perfect electrical hotel. I cannot say whether the kitchens were electric—I suspect not, for the epicurian French palate demands “a taste of the fire”—nor do I know whether the central heating was electrically evoked, being always too overcome by the excessive heat of Continental buildings to have sufficient strength left to enquire about its source, but here I found electricity a silent and inexhaustible servant.

location_standardised: Europe
brief_context: Mentioned in the context of political and social movements.
brief_extract: It is enough to tell you that French women are beginning to think it time France too had an Electrical Association for Women. The chief difficulty would, I think, be to persuade French women into an effort requiring the “team spirit,” for they are individualists in a very particular sense, and it is easier to imagine a Europe unarmed than an Electrical Association such as we have, springing up throughout the land of France. But in spite of all-electric houses and familiarity with electricity as an everyday friend, I have not yet become so electrically blasé that I cannot be thrilled by minor manifestations of this wonder in our midst.

brief_extract: DONALDSON, M.I.C.E., M.I.E.E. A short description of five interesting places in the North Metropolitan Electric Power Supply Company's Area which will be visited by E.A.W. members during the Annual Conference.

location_standardised: Tottenham, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: A factory centre in the southern part of the area.
brief_extract: IT is not an easy matter to give in a small compass an account of the North Metropolitan Electric Power Supply Company's Area, for, not only it is very large, but it varies so much in its character. The southern and more populous part, which is a fringe of the Metropolis, is largely a series of dormitory suburbs, although there are very large factory centres at Tottenham, Edmonton, Enfield and Wembley. It is in this part of the area that housing development has proceeded with very great rapidity and to such an extent that the whole character of the vicinity has completely changed in the last 25 years.

location_standardised: Winchester, Hampshire, England, United Kingdom

brief_extract: The Cathedral and Abbey Church of St. Alban stands on the hill overlooking Verulamium, and is the highest of all the Cathedrals in England, while its length is exceeded only by Winchester, and the structural nave is said to be the longest in the world. The Abbey itself epitomises a long period of history inasmuch as the tower and central parts, which were built in the 11th Century, were largely composed of bricks from Verulamium, while every period of architecture is represented, finishing up with some reconstructions carried out by the late Lord Grimthorpe at the latter end of the 19th Century.

Recently they have become popular, dangerously popular unless due care is taken in their use, and “Sunlight” lamps—mercury vapour, tungsten and carbon arcs—are being more and more installed in bath-rooms and nurseries as a means of providing artificial sunlight through the dark months of our British winter. But as instances to prove the need for knowledge and care in using these lamps that can do so much good, I would mention one man who fell asleep under his sun lamp and was in bed for many weeks whilst his burns healed, and I know of several children who have been given overdoses from amateur sunlight treatment.

brief_extract: IT is curious that the bi-centenary and the centenary of two men whose names have been perpetuated by electrical terms should fall together this year. Watt's steam engine revolutionised the world, and Ampère's work was in part the foundation on which Faraday in 1831 based his discovery of electro-magnetic induction with its far-reaching consequences.

location_standardised: Lancashire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Mentioned in relation to the Lancashire and Cheshire Institute Council.

brief_extract: It was interesting to note that in a crowd of about seventy people only three were women. In France the most important things in life are, apparently, still in the hands of the man. Once the housewife decides to have an electric kitchen, the way is made easy for her.

An exhibition of housecraft should, I think, include all that is new to the craft. Brooms, I thought, are outside the philosophy of an electrical association, but, hope springing eternal, I nevertheless went inside.

location_standardised: Ashford, Kent, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Site of preliminary experimental courses for domestic electrical housecraft.
brief_extract:
Salute to a New Campaign
IN fact, the enthusiastic interest aroused by
the proposed Homeworkers' Electrical House-
craft Certificate was representative of many
different points of view, and our own conviction
that such a campaign was necessary and that elec-
tricity is a possible means towards raising the status
of the domestic worker, found ample confirmation
elsewhere. Preliminary experimental courses have already
been held most successfully at Ashford, Harrogate
and Sutton Coldfield, and with the co-operation
both of mistresses and maids it is hoped that the
classes which will be arranged in the Autumn will
prove equally successful. Wise employers will
realise that improved efficiency has a very definite
value relative to the time taken by classes to attain
that efficiency.

article_title: CONTRASTS - Impressions on a Visit to Africa
brief_extract:
94 THE ELECTRICAL AGE
CONTRASTS
By MARGUERITE B. JACKSON
Impressions on a Visit to Africa
AFRICA the land of mystery and contrasts. Natives following a primitive way of life in grass
huts, far from white men and their so-called
civilisation, are perhaps within a few weeks making use
of the most modern machinery and electrical equipment
and discovering the blessings of a scientific "magic"
more powerful even than that of their "medicine" men.

location_standardised: Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa
brief_context: Mentioned regarding electrical equipment in flats.
article_title: CONTRASTS - Impressions on a Visit to Africa
brief_extract:
This was what I found on my visit to Africa last year. In Cape Town, in contrast to many stately old homes
with slave quarters, well-arranged electrically-equipped
flats are available where the electrical apparatus is
included in the rent of £14 a month. Electricity is an
especial boon here since domestic help is not as easily
obtained as might be imagined, most of the labour being
done by Cape coloured people, now a race distinct from
the real native.

location_standardised: England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Home of the Electrical Association for Women.
article_title: CONTRASTS - Impressions on a Visit to Africa
brief_extract:
That the advantages of electricity are
realised is proved by the increase of 14,000 more electric
cookers in use in 1935 than in 1930, and these are now
being installed in Cape Town homes at the rate of 200
a month. I found the women generally very electrically-
minded, and they were most interested to hear of the
work of the Electrical Association for Women in England
in a short talk I gave at the invitation of the National
Council of Women of South Africa. It was interesting,
too, to find at the Good Hope Housing Scheme for the
lower paid workers that there was great desire among
the tenants for electric cookers and washing machines
which they themselves purchase.

location_standardised: Port Elizabeth, Eastern Cape, South Africa
brief_context: A port of call on the author's trip.
article_title: CONTRASTS - Impressions on a Visit to Africa
brief_extract:
Distribution lines are taken far out into the country
for the service of stations and farms, where in addition
to being used for domestic purposes, electricity is also
used for cold storage and canning. After calling at Port Elizabeth and East London,
where passengers are landed from the ships in baskets,
we arrived at Durban, an attractive seaside town where
the streets are lined by lovely flowering trees, and, in
the middle of hotels, shops, cinemas and traffic lights,
a road sign marked "Nairobi 3,375 miles" surprises
one by its naive implication that this is no very great
distance! A short way from Durban are the Zulu kraals
where one of the accompanying photographs was taken.

location_standardised: Wiltshire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Region where traditional cree'd wheat was found.
brief_extract: The institution and establishment of the Association has been a romantic adventure. First of all journeys were made all over the country to discover how much of the good old English cookery still existed, and amongst other things it was found that in Wiltshire wheat was still "cree'd" (stewed) ready to be made into frumenty for Mothering (Mid-Lent) Sunday, and that schoolboys still catch eels from the Somersetshire rines near Glastonbury, as the tenants of the Glastonbury monks did in days gone by, when they had to give a fixed number of eels during the year as rent. Frumenty and eels are amongst foods that have been more or less neglected, and it is interesting, in view of the present thought devoted to nutrition, to note that both these foods are particularly nutritious and cheap; recipes for both will be given at the end of this article.

Dame Henrietta Barnett
AN APPRECIATION
IT is with the deepest regret that we announce the death on June 10th of Dame Henrietta Octavia Barnett, a Vice-President of the E.A.W., at the age of 85, after a strenuous life of service to the community. Her energy, initiative and idealism have had far-reaching influence, and are perpetuated, among other things, in the University Settlements both in this country and America; in the State Children's Association which softened the cold charity of conditions for Poor Law children; the Children's Country Holiday Movement; and the Garden Suburb at Hampstead which she established. UNEXPECTED ELECTRICITY
ELECTRICITY certainly has exceptional powers. A
strange instance of this is given in the “Utility
News” (Camden, N.J.) that tells of thousands of male
mosquitoes who were lured from a marsh which they
infested to a large electric furnace equipment, where
they met their untimely death in the heat. It is thought
that the mosquitoes mistook the low humming sound
of the furnaces for the call of the female insect, but it
was a sad end to chivalry so to be misled!

DURING the last few years interest in nutrition has
been growing, not only among anxious women trying
by diet to reduce their measurements to fashion’s
decrees, but by organisations endeavouring to improve
the general health of humanity by making it realised
that certain foods have certain effects, and that wise
mixtures of foods eaten will give a greater degree of
physical well-being. In this magazine, Miss Lindsay, of King’s College
of Household and Social Science (University of London),
gives an example of a well and badly balanced menu;
it is a clear indication of how easy it is to choose the
latter and so deprive the eater of a source of potential
good health. The British Medical Association, the Government and
the League of Nations have taken up the question of
nutrition with the particular aim of improving the
physique and functional ability of poorer people who
have little money to spend on food and the greatest need
of good health and resistance to disease.

DOMESTIC ELECTRICITY
IN SWITZERLAND

TEACHING THE FUTURE HOUSEWIFE. A SUMMARY OF " ELEKTRISCHE SCHULKUCHEN "

By LESLIE HEAP, B.Sc., and W.

location_standardised: Zürich, Canton of Zürich, Switzerland
brief_context: Location of Elektrizitätsverwertung, which conducted the study.
brief_extract: SHAND, M.I.E.E. AN exhaustive study of the teaching of electric cooking in schools in Switzerland has recently been made by Elektrizitätsverwertung of Zürich, and the results published with recommendations for practical application under the title of "Elektrische Schulküchen." The subject is a particularly interesting one, and by kind permission of the Elektrizitätsverwertung a summary of the report has been prepared for readers of this magazine, to whom the value of domestic subjects' training for children, under up-to-date conditions, will be apparent. Before proceeding to the Digest itself, some general observations on heavy duty cooking apparatus may be of interest.

location_standardised: England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Comparing apparatus design between Switzerland and England.
brief_extract: When inspecting the cooking equipment of hospitals, hotels, restaurants and schools in Switzerland, one was impressed by the thought that has been devoted to electrical equipment and its arrangement. The Swiss, French and Germans have developed one or two useful forms of appliances, such as the Tilting Cauldron and Tilting Oven, which are especially interesting, while the general design of apparatus is lighter than one is accustomed to in England, and very easy to handle and keep clean. A photograph of a typical large electric kitchen shows the general layout adopted, and also a special appliance called a "Kippkessel," which is used for boiling milk, soup, stews, vegetables and for steaming.

location_standardised: United Kingdom
brief_context: Comparing electricity costs between Switzerland and Britain.
brief_extract: The enthusiasm of both the management and the kitchen staffs for electrical equipment is particularly striking. Although electricity for such purposes is more expensive in Switzerland than it is in Britain, the cost compared with other sources of heat is considered satisfactory, and the convenience of course incomparable. The general question of teaching electric cooking in schools, where the child student is, after all, the future housewife, has received most careful attention, as the following summary will show.

scenery, and avoids the usual descriptive jargon that can

location_standardised: United States
brief_context: Mentioned regarding the Tennessee Valley Development Scheme comparison.
article_title: THE HIGHLANDS OF SCOTLAND. By Hugh Quigley. Photographs by Robert M. Adam.
brief_extract:
It is interesting too to consider the early part of the

book on the economic prospects for the future in con-
junction with an earlier publication of Mr. Quigley's,
"A Plan for the Highlands." In this he propounds a
solution for the grave problems of declining population
and economic difficulties that exist in Scotland by the
formation of a Highland Development Board with a co-
ordinated economic plan covering the whole of the
country, something on the lines of the Tennessee Valley
Development Scheme, which is successfully contending
with rather similar conditions in America. But one
wonders how readily an individualist race would adopt
such an Authority, even under the direction of its own
Nationalists?
